**Page 1**
"""
Review 1 
Rating: 7/10 
Title: Fun and adventurous 
User: careybrandon-41144 — Apr 19, 2021 
A great Disney princess movie filled with wonderful songs and a great story with a pretty 
shocking twist that I honestly never saw coming. 
 
Review 2 
Rating: 7/10 
Title: Definitely Understand the Hype 
User: ryanpersaud-59415 — Nov 14, 2021 
The Good: 
Back in 2013, Frozen became a bona fide phenomenon, on the level that I honestly can't recall 
for an animated movie. Watching this 8 years later as a grown adult, I can say that I totally 
understand why this movie became a phenomenon. 
Frozen has three big things going for it: the songs, the characters, and the interesting subversion 
of tropes. I personally don't love all of them, but the musical numbers give the movie a bouncy, 
fun vibe. The characters are lovable and well written; it's hard not to like someone here, if not the 
entire roster. 
The Bad: 
I don't think the movie does a great job with establishing the central conflict. Despite the first 
portion of the movie covering it, by the time the story gets into it, I just didn't buy the 
relationship between Anna and Elsa until the halfway mark. Anna's motivations are quite poor 
and while I get that we wouldn't have a movie without this conflict, it could have been 
communicated with more patience. 
I also felt the environment lacked a real presence; Arendelle gave me “Asgard” vibes—devoid of 
people, moved on from too fast, not a living world. Maybe it's the cold setting, but I prefer 
fantasy worlds that feel full of life. 
The Ugly: 
Yeah, it's good. I still think Let It Go is a bit overrated and I've seen better-looking animated 
films, but Frozen is solid and fun for the whole family. 
 
Review 3
"""

**Page 2**
"""
Rating: 8/10 
Title: Some People take things WAY too seriously! 
User: calgal84 — Aug 10, 2014 
This is really a lovely, enjoyable cartoon. And it's just that — a lovely, enjoyable cartoon. A 
fairy tale moms and dads can feel happy taking their kids to. 
Is there anything truly remarkable about it? Probably not. Are the songs particularly inventive 
compared to other Disney movies? No, but they are catchy and pretty. The “In Summer” song is 
cute, if a bit oddly placed. 
Some reviewers take this movie way too seriously. Giving it one star because others gave it a 10 
doesn't make you smarter — it just shows you're taking a cartoon too seriously. It's not real. It’s a 
fairy tale. 
I give it an 8. Not perfect, but enjoyable. 
 
Review 4 
Rating: 10/10 
Title: Message of the movie is Love. 
User: mollyjanssen — Jan 9, 2022 
Frozen is a heartwarming movie with fantastic animation. Elsa, Anna, and Olaf make it fun to 
watch. I've seen it several times with my kids and they still think it's a good movie. 
 
Review 5 
Rating: 10/10 
Title: Very Unique 
User: johannafoon — Dec 26, 2021 
A great film that fits in the category of The Lion King, Aladdin, Tarzan, Snow White, 
Pocahontas, and The Little Mermaid. I love the Norwegian cultural influences. Fantastic story, 
beautiful animation — a true Disney classic.

Rating: 10/10 
Title: The directorial 
User: ildarabsalamov — Jan 19, 2022 
The directorial duo managed to make another Disney animated film into an event. They balanced 
responsibilities well, developing a simple story through characters, music, humor, and the 
emotional signature that defines Disney projects. 
The script—loosely based on Andersen's fairy tale—quickly transforms into something unique. 
The writers keep only the dramatic foundation and rebuild everything else. Disney’s strength has 
always been less about plots and more about crafting characters and balancing sad and funny 
moments.

Rating: 10/10 
Title: 10/10 
User: madllen — Jul 27, 2021 
Most Disney movies follow a similar storyline, but this one feels more mature and complex. It’s 
about self-love and self-discovery. It made me shed a tear, and I rewatch it every year with the 
same chills. 
 
Review 11 
Rating: 6/10 
Title: I like warm hugs too 
User: utgard14 — Jan 20, 2014 
Story of two princesses: Elsa, who becomes queen but struggles with her snow powers, and 
Anna, the goofy, lovable younger sister. After an argument in which Elsa reveals her powers 
publicly, she runs away. Anna sets out to bring her back. 
Frozen is good but not great. It’s very loosely adapted from “The Snow Queen.” The sisterly 
bond is touching but not deeply developed. Most of the middle focuses on other characters. 
It reuses familiar Disney tropes and rom-com clichés, though effectively. Olaf, the snowman, is 
entertaining but feels tacked on. The music is “OK” but a bit too Broadway. The animation and 
voice work are solid. Kids and young women may enjoy it more.
"""
